partners.mechanism_chain: APC pathogenic variant (HP:0000001) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:425); APC (HGNC:425) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442) —LEADS_TO→ Intestinal polyposis (HP:0002670); Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575); MLH1 (HGNC:7049) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); MSH2 (HGNC:7443) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); MSH6 (HGNC:7446) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); EPCAM (HGNC:3070) —DISRUPTS→ MSH2 (HGNC:7443); PMS2 (HGNC:9011) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); AXIN2 (HGNC:14177) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442). Loss-of-function mutations in the APC gene disrupt the normal regulation of the Wnt signaling pathway, leading to intestinal polyposis. Colorectal cancer can arise from similar disruptions in APC or through mutations in other Wnt pathway components like CTNNB1, as well as through defects in DNA mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) which indirectly affect Wnt signaling or promote genomic instability that can impact Wnt pathway genes. The convergence is on the dysregulated Wnt signaling pathway, a common driver for both FAP and sporadic colorectal cancer.

### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. colorectal cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.533)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373752)

**Proposed mechanism:** APC pathogenic variant (HP:0000001) —DISRUPTS→ APC (HGNC:425); APC (HGNC:425) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); CTNNB1 (HGNC:2515) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442) —LEADS_TO→ Intestinal polyposis (HP:0002670); Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442) —LEADS_TO→ Colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575); MLH1 (HGNC:7049) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); MSH2 (HGNC:7443) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); MSH6 (HGNC:7446) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); EPCAM (HGNC:3070) —DISRUPTS→ MSH2 (HGNC:7443); PMS2 (HGNC:9011) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442); AXIN2 (HGNC:14177) —DISRUPTS→ Wnt signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-9015442). Loss-of-function mutations in the APC gene disrupt the normal regulation of the Wnt signaling pathway, leading to intestinal polyposis. Colorectal cancer can arise from similar disruptions in APC or through mutations in other Wnt pathway components like CTNNB1, as well as through defects in DNA mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) which indirectly affect Wnt signaling or promote genomic instability that can impact Wnt pathway genes. The convergence is on the dysregulated Wnt signaling pathway, a common driver for both FAP and sporadic colorectal cancer.

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if genetic studies consistently show that pathogenic variants in APC and CTNNB1 are absent in individuals with FAP and colorectal cancer, or if the Wnt signaling pathway is demonstrated to be constitutively active in these conditions irrespective of these genetic alterations. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in APC or CTNNB1 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the Wnt signaling pathway in both FAP and sporadic colorectal cancer provides a unified therapeutic target. Inhibitors of Wnt signaling are under development and could be beneficial for both conditions.

#### 2. esophageal cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.501)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373752)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in WWOX —DISRUPTS→ WWOX (HGNC:12702); WWOX (HGNC:12702) —DECREASES→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-120970); Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (HP:0002090) —LEADS_TO→ WWOX (HGNC:12702); Loss-of-function variant in TGFBR2 —DISRUPTS→ TGFBR2 (HGNC:11708); TGFBR2 (HGNC:11708) —DECREASES→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-120970); TGF-beta signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-120970) —INCREASES→ Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (MONDO:0007576). Loss-of-function variants in WWOX (n6->n1) disrupt its tumor suppressor function and can lead to decreased activity or dysregulation of the TGF-beta signaling pathway (n1->n3), contributing to phenotypes like Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (n4). Similarly, loss-of-function variants in TGFBR2 (n7->n2) directly impair the TGF-beta signaling pathway (n2->n3), which is known to promote tumorigenesis and metastasis in Esophageal Cancer (n3->n5).

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that mutations in WWOX and TGFBR2 in patients with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension are exclusively gain-of-function, or if mutations in WWOX and TGFBR2 in patients with Esophageal Cancer are exclusively gain-of-function, this would falsify the proposed loss-of-function overlap. _(variant: Identification of a common (AF > 1%) pathogenic variant in WWOX or TGFBR2 associated with either disease that is present in gnomAD at a higher frequency than expected for a rare disease variant.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the TGF-beta signaling pathway, or understanding the specific roles of WWOX and TGFBR2 in its dysregulation, could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for both Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension and Esophageal Cancer. For instance, inhibitors of TGF-beta signaling might be explored for their potential to ameliorate vascular remodeling in PAH or suppress tumor growth in esophageal cancer.

#### 3. nystagmus, congenital, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.501)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-373752)

**Proposed mechanism:** HJV (HGNC:5478) —LEADS_TO→ Hereditary Hemochromatosis (MONDO:0011216); HJV (HGNC:5478) —DISRUPTS→ Axon guidance (GO:0007411); ROBO1 (HGNC:10142) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital nystagmus, autosomal recessive (MONDO:0009762); ROBO1 (HGNC:10142) —DISRUPTS→ Axon guidance (GO:0007411); Axon guidance (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Neuronal development (GO:0048666); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Hereditary Hemochromatosis (MONDO:0011216); Neuronal development (GO:0048666) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital nystagmus, autosomal recessive (MONDO:0009762). Loss-of-function mutations in HJV (causative for Hereditary Hemochromatosis) and ROBO1 (causative for congenital nystagmus) both disrupt the conserved biological pathway of axon guidance, which is a critical component of neuronal development. Dysregulation of these fundamental processes in neuronal development leads to the distinct phenotypes of both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** If HJV or ROBO1 mutations were found to be essential for distinct, non-overlapping cellular processes that do not converge on axon guidance or broader neuronal development pathways, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, identification of a common pathogenic variant with high frequency (>5%) in gnomAD within populations relevant to both diseases would challenge the proposed mechanistic link. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of axon guidance pathways in these distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets. Interventions aimed at modulating axon guidance or neuronal development processes might offer a unified approach to treating aspects of both hereditary hemochromatosis and congenital nystagmus, particularly if neurological comorbidities are present in hemochromatosis.

Mutations in DCC disrupt the Netrin-1 signaling pathway, which is crucial for neuronal guidance and spinal development, leading to familial horizontal gaze palsy with progressive scoliosis, 2. The convergence is proposed through the role of Netrin-1 signaling in both neural development and potentially in regulating iron homeostasis indirectly.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that mutations in HJV do not impact the Netrin-1 signaling pathway or related downstream processes, or if experimental models show no phenotypic overlap when HJV and DCC are concurrently modulated, the proposed link would be falsified. _(variant: A common variant (AF > 1%) in HJV or DCC associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of Netrin-1 signaling could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting developmental pathways for both iron overload disorders and neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by gaze palsy and scoliosis.

#### 5. neurooculorenal syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.488)

**Proposed mechanism:** HJV (HGNC:5287) —PRODUCES→ hepcidin (CHEBI:60921); HJV (HGNC:5287) —LEADS_TO→ Iron dysregulation (HP:0011379); hepcidin (CHEBI:60921) —DISRUPTS→ Iron dysregulation (HP:0011379); ROBO1 (HGNC:10242) —DISRUPTS→ Axon guidance (GO:0007411); Axon guidance (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Neurological abnormalities (HP:0000707); ROBO1 (HGNC:10242) —LEADS_TO→ Renal abnormalities (HP:0000114); ROBO1 (HGNC:10242) —LEADS_TO→ Ocular abnormalities (HP:0000477). Loss-of-function mutations in ROBO1 disrupt axon guidance pathways, leading to neurological, renal, and ocular abnormalities in neurooculorenal syndrome (MONDO:0957210). The convergence occurs at the level of cellular processes affected by these distinct genetic origins, ultimately manifesting as complex multi-system disorders.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in HJV or ROBO1 in patients with the other disease would falsify the distinct genetic etiology. Furthermore, if genetic analysis reveals no loss-of-function variants in either HJV or ROBO1 in individuals diagnosed with these respective conditions, this hypothesis would be refuted. _(variant: Exclusion of common loss-of-function variants (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in HJV and ROBO1 in unaffected control populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the distinct roles of HJV and ROBO1 in iron homeostasis and neurodevelopment, respectively, could reveal novel therapeutic targets. For MONDO:0011216, interventions aimed at iron chelation or modulation of hepcidin could be explored. For neurooculorenal syndrome, strategies targeting axon guidance pathways or downstream effects on organ development might offer therapeutic avenues.
